Four gates between a problem and a benefit

Why does an initiative need four human sign-offs when an agent fleet can produce every artifact in between?

A gate is where a human decides on evidence; the review before each gate is what keeps the evidence honest.

Scroll

  1. 1. Hook

Act 1 · Hook

Every gate opens with a review the human runs and never delegates

Agents draft the artifact for each gate. A human checks its claims before deciding whether the work moves forward.

Each stage adds claims. A skipped review catches none, so unchecked claims carry into the next stage.

4 of 4
How the reviewers relate

With 4 gates kept, about 12 of 48 claims reach delivery unreviewed.

Act 2 · Sandbox

Change the assumptions and see which gate the initiative fails at

The opening model fixed the number of claims, the catch rate, review capacity, and reviewer relationship. Change every assumption here.

4 of 4
12 claims
60 percent
16 claims

Reviewer correlation

The model predicts failure at the Investment gate. Reviewers catch 60 percent, and 12 claims reach delivery unreviewed.

Reviewers using the same model share blind spots. The model therefore treats their combined catch rate as one review, not independent evidence.
